title: Tally Marks, Picture Graphs and Bar Graphs
seo_title: Grade 1 Tally Marks and Graphs Worksheets (TEKS 1.8)
standard_text: 1.8A collect, sort, and organize data in up to three categories using models/representations such as tally marks or T-charts; 1.8B use data to create picture and bar-type graphs; 1.8C draw conclusions and generate and answer questions using information from picture and bar-type graphs
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 data worksheets for Texas TEKS 1.8: sort and count, tally charts, picture graphs, bar graphs and how many more or fewer. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Sort things into groups, then count each group.
  • A tally mark is 1. A bundle of 5 tallies (four lines and one across) is 5.
  • In a picture graph, count the pictures. In a bar graph, read the number at the end of the bar.
  • How many more: subtract. In all: add.

Examples

Example

Tally: one bundle and 2 more

5 + 2

Answer: 7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting a bundle of tallies as 1A bundle is 5.
Reading the wrong rowPut your finger on the label first.
Adding when asked how many moreHow many more means subtract.

It makes groups of 5 easy to count.

items.q: How many squares are there?
items.e: Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Count the squares: 1, 2, 3, 4. There are 4 squares.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Count the stars: 1, 2, 3. There are 3 stars.

Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Count the hearts: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. There are 6 hearts.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Count the stars: 1, 2. There are 2 stars.

items.q: Sort the shapes. Which group has 4?
items.e: Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Circles: 3. Triangles: 4. Squares: 2. The triangle group has 4.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Hearts: 4. Squares: 6. Stars: 3. The star group has 3.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Hearts: 6. Triangles: 2. Stars: 4. The heart group has 6.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Triangles: 7. Circles: 4. Stars: 3. 7 is the biggest number, so there are the most triangles.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Circles: 2. Stars: 3. Squares: 4. 4 is the biggest number, so there are the most squares.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Squares: 7. Stars: 2. Hearts: 3. 2 is the smallest number, so there are the fewest stars.
Sort the shapes into groups. Touch each one as you count it. Squares: 6. Hearts: 2. Stars: 5. 2 is the smallest number, so there are the fewest hearts.
Count each group: 4 hearts, 5 circles, 2 stars. Then add: 4 + 5 + 2 = 11. (There are 3 groups, but the question asks for shapes.)
Count each group: 3 circles, 4 squares, 6 hearts. Then add: 3 + 4 + 6 = 13. (There are 3 groups, but the question asks for shapes.)
Count each group: 6 stars, 4 triangles, 5 circles. Then add: 6 + 4 + 5 = 15. (There are 3 groups, but the question asks for shapes.)

sets.title: How many in all, how many more, how many fewer

items.q: How many books did Zoe and Omar read in all?
items.e: Read the bars. Zoe: 5. Omar: 4. In all means add: 5 + 4 = 9 books.
Count the pictures. Swings: 7. Tag: 2. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 7 − 2 = 5. The answer is 5 more kids.

items.q: How many kids are shown in all?
items.e: Count the tally marks. Car: 4. Bike: 3. Bus: 6. Add all three: 4 + 3 + 6 = 13 kids. (There are 3 groups, but the answer is the number of kids.)

items.q: How many fewer days were sunny than cloudy?
items.e: Read the bars. Cloudy: 4. Sunny: 1. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 4 − 1 = 3. The answer is 3 fewer days.

items.q: Sort and count the shapes. Which bar graph matches the shapes?
items.e: First count: Stars 2, Triangles 7, Circles 3. Only graph C has bars at 2, 7 and 3. Graph A has Triangles and Stars switched; B has Triangles 6; D has Stars 3.

items.q: How many votes did Grape and Banana get in all?
items.e: Count the tally marks. Grape: 9. Banana: 2. In all means add: 9 + 2 = 11 votes.

items.q: How many more ladybugs than ants did we see?
items.e: Read the bars. Ladybugs: 8. Ants: 4. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 8 − 4 = 4. The answer is 4 more bugs.

items.q: How many fewer kids have a cat than a fish?
items.e: Read the bars. Fish: 10. Cat: 8. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 10 − 8 = 2. The answer is 2 fewer kids.

items.q: How many votes were there in all?
items.e: Count the tally marks. Red: 6. Yellow: 2. Blue: 5. Add all three: 6 + 2 + 5 = 13 votes. (There are 3 groups, but the answer is the number of votes.)

items.q: How many more kids need to choose popcorn to match grapes?
items.e: Read the bars. Grapes: 6. Popcorn: 4. Popcorn needs to get from 4 up to 6. 6 − 4 = 2, so Popcorn needs 2 more kids.

items.q: How many crows and robins came in all?
items.e: Read the bars. Crow: 10. Robin: 6. In all means add: 10 + 6 = 16 birds.

items.q: How many more dolls than balls are in the box?
items.e: Count the tally marks. Dolls: 7. Balls: 4. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 7 − 4 = 3. The answer is 3 more toys.

items.q: How many fewer shells did Mia find than Leo?
items.e: Read the bars. Leo: 6. Mia: 1. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 6 − 1 = 5. The answer is 5 fewer shells.

items.q: Which bar graph matches the tally chart?
items.e: First count: Yellow 4, Red 6, Green 2. Only graph A has bars at 4, 6 and 2. Graph B has Yellow 5; C has Red 5; D has Red and Yellow switched.

items.q: How many votes did Vanilla and Lemon get in all?
items.e: Count the tally marks. Vanilla: 9. Lemon: 7. In all means add: 9 + 7 = 16 votes.

items.q: How many votes were there in all?
items.e: Read the bars. Banana: 6. Apple: 5. Grape: 8. Add all three: 6 + 5 + 8 = 19 votes. (There are 3 groups, but the answer is the number of votes.)

items.q: How many more bees than ladybugs did we see?
items.e: Count the pictures. Bees: 6. Ladybugs: 4. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 6 − 4 = 2. The answer is 2 more bugs.

items.q: How many fewer kids picked the swings than the slide?
items.e: Count the tally marks. Slide: 8. Swings: 1. Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 8 − 1 = 7. The answer is 7 fewer kids.

items.q: How many more books does Omar need to read to have as many as Lily?
items.e: Read the bars. Lily: 4. Omar: 2. Omar needs to get from 2 up to 4. 4 − 2 = 2, so Omar needs 2 more books.

items.q: How many blue jays and crows came in all?
items.e: Read the bars. Blue Jay: 2. Crow: 10. In all means add: 2 + 10 = 12 birds.
